response: Yes, research suggests that polymorphisms in the beta-adrenergic receptor (ADRB) encoding genes may play a role in Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN). Specifically, it has been found that beta1Gly49 homozygosity and the TACC haplotype of the ADRB2 gene, both of which are loss-of-function genetic variations, may predispose newborns to TTN. This indicates that genetic factors, particularly those related to the beta-adrenergic receptor, may contribute to the development of TTN in newborns.
